title: Retrospective Multicenter Analysis of Genicular Artery Embolization in Germany: Indications, Technique and Outcome
summary:
Background: Some patients suffer from chronic knee pain caused by joint wear (osteoarthritis). One possible treatment involves deliberately closing off small blood vessels in the knee area with the aim of reducing pain. This procedure is already being used at several hospitals in Germany, but has not yet been studied in a consistent way or with a sufficient data basis.
Research question: This study aims to find out which patients have received this treatment so far, how it was performed, and what treatment results were observed.
Methodology: Existing medical records (such as doctors' reports and imaging scans) from patients treated at several German hospitals between 2019 and 2025 will be reviewed. No additional examinations or interviews will take place. All data will be evaluated anonymously, so that no conclusions can be drawn about individual persons.

interventions.name:
Retrospective, multicenter analysis of all patients who underwent genicular artery embolization (GAE) for chronic knee pain/knee osteoarthritis at participating German university hospitals between 01.01.2019 and 31.12.2025.
Only pre-existing clinical routine data from RIS, PACS, and HIS are collect

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Data analysis of patients who received genicular artery embolization (GAE) for treatment-refractory knee pain due to knee osteoarthritis at one of the participating German university hospitals between 01.01.2019 and 31.12.2025, and whose treatment is fully documented in the clinical routine systems (RIS/PACS/HIS).
Exclusion criteria:
Incomplete or non-evaluable documentation of treatment in the clinical routine systems
GAE performed outside the defined time period (before 01.01.2019 or after 31.12.2025)
Genicular artery embolization performed for an indication other than treatment-refractory knee pain/knee osteoarthritis
Patients who have objected to the processing of their data (right to object under the GDNG)
